detail.longDescription: The White House has reversed its decision to restrict the UK AI Safety Institute's access to frontier models from Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI. The policy shift follows direct lobbying led by UK AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, after British officials warned that losing pre-release testing privileges would dismantle the country's regulatory ambitions. Without early access to frontier weights and architectures, independent state auditors cannot effectively evaluate critical risks, catastrophic failure modes, or cyber capabilities before public release. Restoring this access keeps the UK plugged into the primary testing pipeline alongside its American counterparts. However, the dispute exposes the vulnerability of national oversight strategies that rely entirely on foreign technology. When evaluation regimes depend on external political clearance, regulatory independence remains fragile. # AI # UK # TechPolicy # MachineLearning # Technology
